sentence: This project shares magnetic resonance imaging and spectroscopy methods with a broad community through workshops, hands-on courses and a web site.
This project studies how white blood cells and a chemokine make retinal blood vessels leak in diabetes, using cell models, animal models and human samples.
This project stores and shares omic data from brain research projects in one data repository.
This project builds a biologic therapy that suppresses the immune response in a targeted way and promotes regulatory T cells to help transplants last.
This project studies how T cells multiply in early type 1 diabetes and whether this shows how active the disease is.
This project studies immune cells from patients and healthy people to find what drives a rare disease and how a redox sensor changes B cells.
This project builds a vector that restores a missing enzyme in stem cell-derived neurons and tests whether it works safely in mice with the disorder.
This project builds AI tools that predict breast cancer risk from imaging and tests how well they hold up on unseen image protocols.
This project builds tiny particles that hold chemotherapy drugs and can cross the blood brain barrier to treat brain tumors like glioblastoma.
This project studies how a tick-borne parasite changes the red blood cells it infects and how its proteins interact with the red blood cell cytoskeleton.
This project uses a mouse model to study how loss of one gene causes the brain changes and seizures seen in focal cortical dysplasia.
This project builds a framework for finding, testing and developing treatments for honey bees, which suffer losses from parasites and pathogens.
This project studies how enzymes that use iron and oxygen carry out chemical reactions that build compounds with biological activity.
This project studies how often persistent infections with the virus occur, what causes them and what the virus is like, using virology, immunology and genomics.
This project studies how an enzyme made by a bacterium helps it cause disease and whether blocking it could work as a therapy.
This project improves ways to turn induced pluripotent stem cells into dopamine cells that could be used in personalized cell therapy for Parkinson’s disease.
This project tests whether a brain protein could be a target for medicines to treat stimulant use disorder.
This project studies how bile acids and a bile acid receptor shape the behavior of gut macrophages in colitis and colon cancer.
This project uses a rodent model of alcohol dependence to link epigenetic changes in key genes to cognitive and pain symptoms of withdrawal.
This project offers nanotechnology tools and services to kidney researchers so they can deliver treatments to specific cells and regions in the kidney.
